title: Manitoba Invites 526 Workers in Draw 283, Led by Manufacturing and Farm Jobs
excerpt: The province's 22nd draw of 2026 sent 448 of its 526 Letters of Advice to Apply to people already working in Manitoba in natural resources, agriculture, manufacturing and utilities, with 60 days to file a full nomination application.
body:
• Manitoba issued 526 Letters of Advice to Apply in Expression of Interest Draw #283 on November 5, 2026, its 22nd draw of the year.
  • The largest share, 448 letters, went to people already working in Manitoba in natural resources, agriculture, manufacturing and utilities occupations.
  • Another 78 letters went to candidates directly invited under strategic recruitment initiatives, led by Regional Communities with 30.
  • Invited candidates have up to 60 days to submit a complete application for provincial nomination; 49 of the 526 declared a valid Express Entry profile.

Manitoba has invited 526 candidates to apply for provincial nomination in its latest immigration draw. The Manitoba Provincial Nominee Program (MPNP) issued the Letters of Advice to Apply in Expression of Interest Draw #283 on November 5, 2026, according to the province's official draw notice.

Where the invitations went

The draw was occupation-led. Under the Skilled Worker in Manitoba pathway, 448 letters went to profiles declaring current employment in Manitoba in two broad occupational categories: natural resources, agriculture and related production occupations, and occupations in manufacturing and utilities. Those categories span middle management and supervisors in farming, mining, forestry and manufacturing, equipment and machine operators, and processing and harvesting labourers, CIC News reported in its breakdown of the draw.

The remaining 78 letters went to Skilled Worker candidates, in Manitoba and overseas, who had been directly invited by the MPNP under a strategic recruitment initiative. Regional Communities accounted for 30 of those invitations, followed by Employer Services with 20, the Francophone Community with 12, Ethnocultural Communities with 11, and the Temporary Public Policy for prospective nominee candidates with 5.

Of the 526 letters issued, 49 went to candidates who declared a valid Express Entry profile number and job seeker validation code — the group that can move fastest at the federal stage once nominated.

What happens next for invitees

A Letter of Advice to Apply is an invitation, not a nomination. Each invited candidate has up to 60 days to submit a complete application for provincial nomination to the MPNP. Once nominated, a candidate can request a work permit support letter from the MPNP for a federal work permit application, and may be eligible for a bridging open work permit once they have applied for permanent residence.

The province's notice carries two cautions for this round. Expressions of Interest from Skilled Worker candidates were considered only if they were directly invited under a strategic recruitment initiative or the temporary public policy. And candidates working in a regulated occupation were selected on the basis that they are fully licensed to work in Manitoba; the MPNP warns it may refuse full applications from candidates who are not actually working in the regulated occupation or cannot prove they have completed the licensing steps, and suggests such candidates consider declining the letter.

For workers already employed in Manitoba's farms, plants and utilities, Draw #283 was one of the year's larger occupation-specific rounds. For everyone else in the pool, the draw's message is narrower: this round rewarded current Manitoba employment in two industrial categories and direct recruitment invitations, not general scores.
